elements.brief_element: The system is an offline evaluation harness that executes scenario suites against an AI system and grades the resulting outputs.
elements.brief_evidence: “We need a diagram of how our offline evaluation harness executes scenario suites against an AI system and grades the results.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies the purpose as “An offline evaluation harness that runs pinned scenario suites in bounded isolated workers” and describes execution, grading, scorecard assembly, comparison, retention, and baseline promotion.
elements.note: The domain and overall purpose are communicated accurately.

elements.brief_element: Every run starts from a pinned suite.
elements.brief_evidence: “Each run starts from a pinned suite…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies section “1 · Pinned run inputs,” the “Pinned suite” component, and the “Pinned-input run startup” flow leading through the run fingerprint to the suite scheduler.
elements.note: The pinned suite is clearly shown as the run's starting input.

elements.brief_element: The pinned suite contains frozen scenario definitions.
elements.brief_evidence: “Each run starts from a pinned suite containing frozen scenario definitions…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction reports a “Pinned suite” and an “Immutable scenarios rule” stating that wording changes create a new scenario version, but it does not report an explicit statement that the suite contains frozen scenario definitions.
elements.note: Immutability is strongly implied, but the exact suite-content relationship is not directly recovered.

elements.brief_element: The pinned run includes a fingerprint of the tested revision.
elements.brief_evidence: “…and a fingerprint of the tested revision…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies a “Run fingerprint” and later uses fingerprints for compatibility checks, but it does not state that the tested revision is one of the fingerprint's constituent fields.
elements.note: The fingerprint exists, but this specific input to it is omitted.

elements.brief_element: The pinned run fingerprint includes the tested configuration.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: No matching reconstruction entry states that configuration is included in the run fingerprint.
elements.note: The fingerprint is recovered only as an undifferentiated value.

elements.brief_element: The pinned run fingerprint includes prompt versions.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: No matching reconstruction entry states that prompt versions are included in the run fingerprint.
elements.note: This fingerprint constituent is absent from the reconstruction.

elements.brief_element: The pinned run fingerprint includes rubric versions.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: No matching reconstruction entry states that rubric versions are included in the run fingerprint.
elements.note: This fingerprint constituent is absent from the reconstruction.

elements.brief_element: Scenario wording changes invalidate historical comparisons.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction reports the rule “Wording changes create a new scenario version” and also reports that only matching fingerprints may be compared, but it does not explicitly recover the causal statement that wording changes invalidate historical comparisons.
elements.note: The prescribed response to wording changes survives, while the historical-comparison rationale is only implicit.

elements.brief_element: Scenarios receive new versions rather than being edited in place.
elements.brief_evidence: “…scenarios receive new versions instead of being edited in place.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The “Immutable scenarios rule” says, “Wording changes create a new scenario version,” and the constraints repeat that wording is immutable within a version.
elements.note: The versioning and immutability rule is transmitted clearly.

elements.brief_element: A scheduler fans scenario work out to workers.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies a “Suite scheduler” whose responsibility is to schedule work and a flow from it to the “Bounded worker pool.”
elements.note: Scheduling ownership and direction are clear.

elements.brief_element: The worker pool is bounded.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies a component explicitly labeled “Bounded worker pool” and lists bounded execution as a constraint.
elements.note: The execution concurrency boundary is explicit.

elements.brief_element: Workers target an isolated instance of the system under test.
elements.brief_evidence: “…targeting an isolated instance of the system under test…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies “Isolated SUT” and states that workers execute ordered scenario steps against it.
elements.note: The target and its isolation boundary are recovered.

elements.brief_element: The harness never targets the shared production instance.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The execution-workers evidence states, “The shared production instance is never targeted,” and the same requirement appears in the constraints.
elements.note: The production-safety boundary is explicit.

elements.brief_element: Each worker performs a scenario's steps in order.
elements.brief_evidence: “Each worker performs a scenario's steps in order…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction says workers “execute ordered scenario steps,” and its execution flow repeats that ordering.
elements.note: The required execution sequence is unambiguous.

elements.brief_element: Each worker captures the full transcript.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The execution-workers component and constraints explicitly say workers capture the “full transcript + final artifact.”
elements.note: Transcript capture is explicit.

elements.brief_element: Each worker captures the final artifact.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The execution-workers component and execution flow explicitly include capture of the final artifact.
elements.note: Artifact capture is explicit.

elements.brief_element: Infrastructure failures trigger retries.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The “Infrastructure fault” component and failure path state that a captured result classified as an infrastructure fault is retried.
elements.note: The trigger, classification, and retry outcome are all recovered.

elements.brief_element: Failures caused by the tested system's behavior are recorded.
elements.brief_evidence: “…while failures caused by the tested system's behavior are recorded…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies “Product behavior failure” and states “Product behavior: record and continue.”
elements.note: Product-caused failure handling is accurately separated from infrastructure handling.

elements.brief_element: After recording a tested-system behavior failure, the worker continues.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The product-behavior failure path ends in “Record and continue,” and the associated constraint says processing continues.
elements.note: The non-terminal outcome is clear, although the reconstruction says evaluation or processing continues rather than always naming the same worker.

elements.brief_element: Results preserve the distinction between infrastructure failures and product regressions.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction has an explicit “Outcome separation” stage and an “Outcome-separation policy” preserving distinct infrastructure-fault and product-behavior outcomes.
elements.note: This is one of the clearest transmitted behaviors.

elements.brief_element: Operational faults must not masquerade as product regressions.
elements.brief_evidence: “…so operational faults cannot masquerade as product regressions.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction quotes the policy that results preserve the distinction “so operational faults cannot masquerade as regressions.”
elements.note: The operational purpose of outcome separation is explicit.

elements.brief_element: Completed scenarios enter grading immediately.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction reports a route labeled “completed scenario” entering the “Grading dispatcher” directly from the execution/outcome area.
elements.note: The direct transition is recovered; the word “immediately” is supported by the absence of an intervening batch stage.

elements.brief_element: Independent graders score separate criteria.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies “Criterion graders” that independently grade separate criteria and a dispatcher route labeled “criteria.”
elements.note: Criterion separation and grader independence are explicit.

elements.brief_element: Separate criterion graders operate concurrently.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The grading section is titled “Evidence-backed concurrent grading,” and its policy says “Concurrent, independent grading.”
elements.note: Concurrency is explicitly communicated.

elements.brief_element: Grading concurrency is governed by one global concurrency limit.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction quotes, “Separate criteria run under one global concurrency limit.”
elements.note: The global operational limit is exact.

elements.brief_element: An artifact-only grader receives the artifact without the original request.
elements.brief_evidence: “…while an artifact-only grader receives no original request…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction correctly reports an “artifact only” route and repeatedly states that the artifact-only grader “never sees the original request,” but one component responsibility incorrectly says it “Reviews only the original request artifact.”
elements.note: The dominant reading is correct, but the phrase “original request artifact” introduces a localized ambiguity about what the grader actually receives.

elements.brief_element: Withholding the original request from the artifact-only grader avoids anchoring on it.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: No matching reconstruction entry explains that request withholding is intended to avoid anchoring.
elements.note: The isolation mechanism survives, but its stated rationale does not.

elements.brief_element: Every verdict includes supporting evidence.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The grading flow produces “verdict + evidence,” followed by an “Evidence present?” check, and retention includes “Verdicts + evidence.”
elements.note: Evidence is visibly part of both validation and retention.

elements.brief_element: A verdict without evidence is invalid.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The grading policy explicitly states, “Missing evidence invalidates the verdict.”
elements.note: The validation rule is exact.

elements.brief_element: An invalid verdict caused by missing evidence is retried.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The missing-evidence failure path says the verdict is invalidated and retried once.
elements.note: The board adds the bounded detail “once,” which is compatible with the brief's unspecified retry count.

elements.brief_element: If the evidence retry also fails, the verdict is flagged.
elements.brief_evidence: “…and is flagged if the retry also fails.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The concurrent-grading policy and failure path state “retry once → flag if still invalid.”
elements.note: The terminal outcome after failed recovery is exact.

elements.brief_element: An assembler merges valid verdicts into a scorecard.
elements.brief_evidence: “An assembler merges valid verdicts into a scorecard…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: A “valid” grading result enters “Verdict assembler,” whose output is “merge”d into “Run scorecard · stability.”
elements.note: Validity gating, assembly ownership, and destination are all clear.

elements.brief_element: The assembled scorecard is compared with a chosen baseline.
elements.brief_evidence: “…and compares it with a chosen baseline…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The scorecard flows through “compare” to “Fingerprints match?” while the “Chosen baseline” supplies a fingerprint into that compatibility stage.
elements.note: The baseline relationship is recoverable, though the scorecard-to-baseline data path is represented via the compatibility check.

elements.brief_element: The comparison identifies movements that cross a defined threshold.
elements.brief_evidence: “…narrating movements that cross a defined threshold.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies a “Threshold movement” component after a matching-fingerprint decision, but does not report an explicit configured or defined threshold value or threshold definition.
elements.note: Threshold-crossing movement is visible, but the fact that the threshold is defined as a comparison parameter is softened.

elements.brief_element: The harness narrates threshold-crossing movements.
elements.brief_evidence: “…narrating movements that cross a defined threshold.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: No matching reconstruction entry identifies a narration or narrative-generation responsibility for movements. The reconstruction instead introduces swing detection and rerun handling after comparison.
elements.note: This is the most consequential missing behavior in the comparison stage.

elements.brief_element: Comparison is permitted only when both runs have the same fingerprint.
elements.brief_evidence: “Comparison is permitted only when both runs share the same fingerprint.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies “Fingerprints match?” and explicitly states, “Only matching fingerprints may be compared.”
elements.note: The compatibility gate is clear and exact.

elements.brief_element: The harness retains every artifact.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The “Audit & retention” section includes an “Artifacts” store, and the constraints state that artifacts are retained.
elements.note: Retention is explicit, although the reconstruction notes that the individual ingestion arrow is not drawn.

elements.brief_element: The harness retains every transcript.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The “Audit & retention” section includes a “Transcripts” store, and the constraints state that transcripts are retained.
elements.note: Retention is explicit, despite the missing individual ingestion arrow.

elements.brief_element: The harness retains every verdict.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The audit section includes “Verdicts + evidence,” and the reconstruction says every run remains re-examinable.
elements.note: Verdict retention is explicit.

elements.brief_element: Retention allows disputed scores to be re-examined.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The audit policy states, “Every run remains re-examinable when a score is disputed.”
elements.note: The retention purpose is recovered exactly.

elements.brief_element: Promoting a run makes it the baseline.
elements.brief_evidence: “…and promoting a run makes it the baseline…”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The baseline lifecycle shows “Promote compatible run” followed by “becomes” and “Chosen baseline.”
elements.note: The state transition is clear.

elements.brief_element: The promoted baseline is used by future runs.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The baseline lifecycle shows “Chosen baseline” — “used by” → “Future compatible runs.”
elements.note: Future use is explicit.

elements.brief_element: Only future runs compatible with the promoted baseline use it.
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The destination is explicitly labeled “Future compatible runs,” and the promotion source is labeled “Promote compatible run.”
elements.note: Compatibility is preserved at both promotion and future-use boundaries.

elements.brief_element: The main end-to-end orchestration moves a pinned run through bounded execution, evidence-backed grading, compatible baseline comparison, and retention/promotion while preserving the infrastructure-versus-product distinction.
elements.brief_evidence: “The diagram should make clear how a pinned run moves from bounded execution through evidence-backed grading and compatible baseline comparison, while keeping infrastructure failures distinct from product regressions.”
elements.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction provides ordered flows from pinned suite and fingerprint to scheduler, bounded worker pool and isolated SUT, captured-result classification, completed-scenario grading, evidence validation, verdict assembly, scorecard comparison behind a fingerprint gate, audit retention, and compatible baseline promotion. Infrastructure and product failures have separate routes and outcomes.
elements.note: The primary architecture and operational story are actionable end to end. The main loss occurs inside the post-comparison behavior, where narration is omitted and unsupported swing-rerun behavior is introduced.

unsupported_claims.claim: Threshold or run-to-run movements trigger comparable-run swing detection and bounded scenario reruns.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies “5a · Swing detection & retries,” “Comparable-run swing?,” “Bounded retry allowance,” and a dashed “re-run scenario” loop to isolated execution.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief requires narration of movements crossing a defined threshold. It does not state that score movements trigger scenario reruns or define a swing-detection recovery loop.

unsupported_claims.claim: The harness records observed attempt variance for comparison-triggered reruns.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction includes “Observed attempt variance,” a “Variance recording” flow, and a “retain variance” route into audit storage.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief requires retention of artifacts, transcripts, and verdicts, but says nothing about rerun-attempt variance or variance as a separate comparison artifact.

unsupported_claims.claim: A persistently variable result is marked unstable on the scorecard.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction identifies “Unstable result,” says it returns instability to “Run scorecard · stability,” and states that persistent instability is marked on the scorecard.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief contains no unstable-result state or scorecard stability designation.

unsupported_claims.claim: Unstable results are never silently averaged.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction quotes a comparison contract saying a result that remains unstable is “never silently averaged.”
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief specifies neither averaging behavior nor a prohibition on averaging repeated attempts.

unsupported_claims.claim: The artifact-only grader reviews an “original request artifact.”
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The “Artifact-only grader” component responsibility says it “Reviews only the original request artifact,” although other reconstruction entries say it never sees the original request.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief says the grader receives no original request. Calling its input an “original request artifact” is not supported and creates ambiguity about whether request content is supplied.

unsupported_claims.claim: The run scorecard specifically contains stability information.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction names the component “Run scorecard · stability.”
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief defines a scorecard and threshold-crossing movement narration, but does not specify a stability field or stability-focused scorecard.

verdict.strongest_transmitted_behavior: The board most strongly transmits the execution and outcome-separation path: a pinned run is scheduled into a bounded worker pool against an isolated non-production SUT, ordered steps capture transcripts and artifacts, infrastructure faults are retried, and product-behavior failures are recorded while processing continues.
verdict.most_consequential_loss: The required post-comparison narration of movements crossing a defined threshold is not recovered. It is replaced by an unsupported swing-detection, bounded-rerun, variance-retention, and unstable-scorecard subsystem, which could lead engineers to implement materially different comparison behavior.
verdict.overall_summary: The reconstruction recovers the complete high-level system shape and nearly all critical paths: pinned inputs, immutable scenario versioning, bounded isolated execution, ordered capture, infrastructure/product outcome separation, concurrent evidence-backed grading, missing-evidence retry and flagging, verdict assembly, fingerprint-gated comparison, audit retention, and compatible baseline promotion. Supporting fingerprint composition details and the anti-anchoring rationale are omitted. More importantly, threshold-crossing movements are shown but their required narration is absent, while a substantial unsupported swing-rerun and instability mechanism is added. The main end-to-end flow remains accurate and usable for engineering discussion, but the comparison stage would require clarification before implementation.
